dedupe_keys.name: taiwan remote area mountain and disaster prevention mobile coverage programmes improved sites subsidies and designated areas moda

description: The Ministry of Digital Affairs publishes open data on programmes that extend and harden mobile coverage outside Taiwan's cities. The mountain mobile communication improvement plan lists 150 new or optimised coverage points (2020 to 2023) in forest reserves, national parks and other protected land. Each point has its type, trail name, lead operator, technology, flags for Indigenous communities and statutory remote areas, the operators served, the location of the phone signal marker sign and coordinates. A later file adds 26 mountain sites and trails with coordinates. Subsidy tables by year, county, district and operator cover base stations built in remote areas, the programme to strengthen disaster-prevention and relief mobile communications (156 rows), and rural broadband access infrastructure. Lists give the villages designated as remote areas, the statutory universal-service areas and the villages where universal data service is required. Coverage: Taiwan's mountain, remote and Indigenous areas. Format and access: CSV from the national open data portal, free under the Open Government Data License. Caveats: these are programme records, not measured coverage maps; the subsidy files give amounts, not site capacities; files were updated between 2023 and 2025 and may not include later rounds. Simulation uses: locating hardened and gap-filling sites for mountain rescue and typhoon or earthquake communication scenarios, and relating subsidy spending to rural coverage. Related records: the KCA mobile base stations in mountain areas (South Korea) and the NCC base station statistics for Taiwan give comparable site counts; the NCDR public alert platform for Taiwan gives the hazard messaging that such sites carry.
name: Taiwan remote-area, mountain and disaster-prevention mobile coverage programmes: improved sites, subsidies and designated areas (MODA)
notes: Metadata read from the data.gov.tw catalogue export on 2026-09-26 (datasets 160533, 173234, 173233, 161787, 161771, 161777, 161761, 157735). The 150 and 156 counts are the catalogue's recorded data volume. Files were not opened.
